Current WRRF distributed control systems (DCS), supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems, and utility data management systems (DMS) rely on personnel with specialized process knowledge to make manual setpoint adjustments. The slow evolution of advanced control schemes has been impeded for decades by the historical lack of reliable sensors (Love and Bott 2001; Ohmura et al. 2019) and the lack of accurate models for a variety of treatment processes at full-scale WRRFs. Traditional mechanistic modeling has been used to capture full-scale process dynamics; however, these models do not provide the precision needed for advanced control (Newhart et al. 2019). For example, feedforward (FF), as well as FB, control strategies often fail because (i) downstream treatment is not accurately modeled for all conditions, and (ii) single-sensor control strategies are inadequate. Even novel, emerging treatment process Applications included in this project have used simple FB and rule-based controllers despite the limitations noted previously. Through this project, the project team developed and demonstrated advanced data-driven control schemes which are reflective of true full-scale performance based on multiple sources of historical data to overcome the assumptions and limitations of mechanistic, PI, or rule-based controllers.
